full_judgment: 3. Facts in short are as follows: property in suit originally belonged to one Jnan Ranjan who gifted the same to his son Mono Ranjan Banerjee with an authority to make further construction (ext. 8). Mono Ranjan recorded his name in the Municipality in 1923-24 Ext. 5 and the Municipality sanctioned his plan for further construction on 4.10.29. Mono Ranjan died leaving behind three sons namely Sattaya Ranjan Banerjee, Kumud Ranjan Banerjee and Shanti Ranjan Banerjee and his wife Brinda Banerjee. It appears that this house was taken on lease in 1926-27 by the Dhaka Nawab Estate. The plaintiffs husband was an officer of the estate. He occupied one portion of the building living there with his family. In 1947 the office of the Nawab Estate was shifted to a different place. The plaintiffs husband, however, continued occupation of the entire suit premises as monthly tenant under the proforma defendants 4 to 6 namely Sattya Ranjan, Kumud Ranjan and Shanti Ranjan Banerjee. The Banerjees left the then East Pakistan and asked the Evacuee Property Management Board to take over the property for management in their absence whereupon a Gazettee Notification was made by the Government under section 8(1) of Act XXIV of 1951 dated 31.12.53. Thereafter the plaintiffs husband paid rent upto 1954 to the Evacuee Property Management Committee and recognised him as tenant Ext. 1 series. In 1954 the plaintiff started paying rent in her name and continued payment of rent from January 1954 to 1969.
